text:
maria: Heads up — after the eu-west node bump last night I'm seeing batch-window length and queue depth increase for a subset of GPU pools. Headroom panel flipped negative on a few shards around 02:10 UTC.

aj: saw that too, noticed avg_batch_size jumped and tail latency for short requests increased. Did autoscaler behave normally (no scale-down/grow noise)?
	maria: autoscaler logs show normal activity, no flapping. But the batch-window distribution shifted — more 512+ token requests landing in the same pool.
	tariq: can you share the grafana panel link and a prom query snapshot?
	maria: link: https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/db/headroom?panelId=7&orgId=1&from=now-3h&to=now (filters: region=eu-west, pool=dedicated-gpu-1)

	Prom query I grabbed for queue depth over pools:
	```
	sum by (pool) (rate(model_request_queue_depth[1m]))
	```
	and batch window 95th percentile:
	```
	histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_window_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
	```

	aj: thanks. The shape matches what I saw — queue depth spikes correlate with a shift in request length. Could be traffic profile change or a routing policy routing long chat sessions to the wrong pool.
	maria: we didn't change routing policies. We did roll a kernel update to runtime yesterday (small scheduler tweak). Could that change batching behavior?
	tariq: possible — scheduler tweak changed how the runtime groups request lengths for batching. If larger sequence lengths are batched together, KV cache eviction and memory pressure could reduce effective parallelism and increase window.
	observability-bot: alert triggered: HEADROOM_NEGATIVE pool=dedicated-gpu-1 at 2024-02-21T02:12:04Z (rule: headroom < 0 for 2m).
	aj: action plan: 1) reproduce with synthetic load targeting eu-west dedicated-gpu-1 2) add temporary dashboard panels for per-model request_size and per-pool batch_count 3) if kernel change is culprit, roll runtime to previous image in a canary pool.
	maria: I'm running a synthetic job now that replays yesterday's traffic slice (same user distribution + long sessions). Will attach logs.

	Synthetic run snippet (k8s job):
	```
	kubectl run synth-batch-replay --image=internal/synth:latest --restart=OnFailure -- /bin/replay --trace slice_20240220.json --target-pool dedicated-gpu-1
	```

	tariq: while that's running, can we tune alerts to avoid noisy paging? Current HEADROOM_NEGATIVE fires on 1m; we should debounce to 5m and correlate with sustained queue_growth. Proposed alert rule:
	```
	ALERT HeadroomDegraded
	  IF min_over_time(headroom{job=\"headroom_exporter\"}[5m]) < 0 and increase(model_request_queue_depth[5m]) > 10
	  FOR 10m
	  LABELS { severity = \"page\" }
	  ANNOTATIONS { summary = \"Sustained negative headroom in {{ $labels.pool }}\" }
	```

	aj: +1 on debounce and requiring queue growth. otherwise we'll page on short transient reorders.
	maria: synth job shows same spike after a few minutes, batch_count per GPU increased and per-request latency climbs. Logs point to kernel scheduler grouping by request_size upper bound.
	tariq: can you paste the scheduler flag snapshot? We added `--batching-window-ms=12 --group-by=prefix_len` yesterday. Maybe group-by=prefix_len groups long sequences together.
	maria: exact flags from canary node: `--batching-window-ms=12 --group-by=prefix_len`
	aj: quick mitigation: revert canary nodes to `--group-by=model_id` so long sessions are distributed across groups by model, not length. That should reduce per-batch variance.
	maria: I'm going to patch one pool with reverted flags and watch headroom. Will report in 10m.
	observability-bot: deploy started for runtime-image: runtime:v2024-02-19 (canary pool dedicated-gpu-1a)

	(8 minutes later)
	maria: reverted canary to group-by=model_id for pool dedicated-gpu-1a — headroom recovered to positive, queue depth and 95p batch-window dropped.
	aj: nice. Next steps: 1) roll change to other eu-west pools 2) schedule root cause PR to revisit default grouping in scheduler 3) update dashboard to show `group_by` label on batch panels for easier triage.
	tariq: also add a small migration test that replays mixes of long/short sessions against new scheduler flags before rollout.
	maria: agreed. I'll open a postmortem-lite with timeline, include prom/grafana snapshots and the synth job artifact.
	aj: for alerts I'll make a PR to bump FOR to 10m and add the queue growth clause. Also add an annotation linking to the synth job for runbook.
	maria: thanks team, closing this thread once PRs are up.
	(reacts: :thumbsup:)
